::: {#thm-subset-transitive}
#### Subsets of subsets

Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets.
If $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq C$, then $A \subseteq C$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Suppose $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq C$, and let $a \in A$.
Since $A \subseteq B$, $a \in B$ (@def-subset).
Since $B \subseteq C$, $a \in C$.
So every element of $A$ is in $C$, and $A \subseteq C$.

:::

:::
